notes.source: Federal Register doc. 2024-14974 (2024-07-09), SEC notice of amendments to FINRA Rule 8312 (BrokerCheck Disclosure), “FINRA’s BrokerCheck Tool”
notes.evidence: The information that FINRA releases to the public through BrokerCheck is derived from CRD, the central licensing and registration system that FINRA operates

notes.front: Before opening an account, an investor wants to see a broker’s registrations and any regulatory history. Which free FINRA tool should she use?
notes.back: BrokerCheck.
notes.choices:
A) BrokerCheck
B) Form U5
C) The Firm Element
notes.choicesExplained: B: Form U5 is a termination filing, not a public search tool. C: the Firm Element is continuing education.
notes.explanation: BrokerCheck is designed to help investors make informed choices about the people and firms they do business with.
notes.source: Federal Register doc. 2024-14974 (2024-07-09), SEC notice of amendments to FINRA Rule 8312 (BrokerCheck Disclosure), “FINRA’s BrokerCheck Tool”
notes.evidence: BrokerCheck is a free tool available on FINRA's website that is designed to help investors make informed choices about the associated persons and broker-dealer firms with which they conduct or may conduct business.

notes.front: Under FINRA Rule 2267, what must member firms give customers, and how often?
notes.back: FINRA’s website address and information about BrokerCheck, at least once every calendar year.
notes.explanation: Exceptions cover firms with no customers and introducing firms whose carrying firm complies for them.
notes.source: Federal Register doc. E8-31204 (2009-01-02), SEC notice of FINRA’s proposed Rule 2267, section I
notes.evidence: require member firms, with certain exceptions, to provide customers with FINRA's Web site address and information regarding FINRA's BrokerCheck program at least once every calendar year.
notes.validAsOf: 2009-01-02 · FINRA Rule 2267 as proposed in 2009; later amendments not checked

notes.front: Under FINRA Rule 2263, when must a member give an associated person the required arbitration disclosures?
notes.back: Whenever it asks them to sign an initial or amended Form U4, or otherwise acknowledge an amendment in writing.
notes.explanation: The disclosure explains that Form U4 contains a predispute arbitration clause and advises the person to read it.
notes.source: Federal Register doc. E9-9372 (2009-04-24), SEC notice of FINRA’s proposed Rules 1010 and 2263, “Purpose”
notes.evidence: a member must provide the required arbitration disclosures whenever a member asks an associated person, pursuant to proposed FINRA Rule 1010 (as described above), to manually sign an initial or amended Form U4
notes.validAsOf: 2009-04-24 · FINRA Rule 2263 as proposed in 2009; later amendments not checked

notes.front: Can an arbitration decision be appealed like a court judgment?
notes.back: No: a party may only seek to vacate an award on narrow statutory grounds.
notes.explanation: So arbitration decisions are unlikely to be overturned.
notes.source: Investor.gov glossary, “Arbitration and Mediation”
notes.evidence: Unlike in litigation, however, arbitration decisions cannot be appealed; a party may seek to vacate (or overturn) an award on narrow statutory grounds. Thus, arbitration decisions are unlikely to be overturned.

notes.front: Under FINRA Rule 2060, what may a member not do with information about securities ownership received as paying agent, transfer agent or trustee?
notes.back: Use it to solicit purchases, sales or exchanges, except at the request and on behalf of the issuer.
notes.explanation: The rule was part of the original rulebook, and its text had not been amended since it was adopted.
notes.source: Federal Register doc. E9-25872 (2009-10-28), SEC notice of FINRA’s proposed Rules 2060 and 5290, “Proposed FINRA Rule 2060”
notes.evidence: a member who receives information as to the ownership of securities while acting in the capacity of paying agent, transfer agent, trustee or otherwise shall under no circumstances make use of the information for soliciting purchases, sales or exchanges except at the request and on behalf of the issuer.

notes.front: Why did the MSRB amend Rule G-3 in 2022 to make the Regulatory Element annual for dealers?
notes.back: To align its continuing education rules with the SEC-approved amendments to FINRA Rules 1210 and 1240.
notes.explanation: The MSRB sets professional qualification standards for dealers and municipal advisors under the Exchange Act.
notes.source: Federal Register doc. 2022-19678 (2022-09-13), SEC notice of amendments to MSRB Rule G-3, “Purpose”
notes.evidence: The purpose of the proposed rule change is to align certain obligations under MSRB Rule G-3 for dealers with Commission approved amendments to FINRA Rules 1210, on registration requirements, and 1240, on continuing education requirements

notes.front: Under MSRB Rule G-10, what must dealers tell customers once every calendar year?
notes.back: That they are registered with the SEC and the MSRB, the MSRB’s website address, and that an MSRB investor brochure is available.
notes.explanation: The brochure describes the protections MSRB rules may provide and how to file a complaint with a regulator.
notes.source: Federal Register doc. 2021-17830 (2021-08-20), SEC notice of proposed amendments to MSRB Rule G-10, “Purpose”
notes.evidence: (i) A statement that the regulated entity is registered with the SEC and the MSRB; (ii) The website address for the MSRB; and (iii) A statement as to the availability to the customer or municipal advisory client of a brochure
